text:
i have the desire to start a biotech company. why? 
1) i have the intuition that academia is not the right culture for me. why? With the caveat that I have a small sample size, my experience in academia has been that people are not working on ambitious projects.  What I have found in industries is that people are working on ambitious projects projects. this is what i want. For whatever reason, perhaps due to outstanding academic culture or funding incentives or idrc and it doesn't matter as much as the fact of the matter. I'm open to having my mind changed on the culture of academia. 
1a) why is culture important? i think it really shapes what you want (mimetic desire) (im not gonna larp and say ive read any René Girard but i get the idea) . Anecdotally, i go to cornell, and i see how this plays out with the kinds of careers that people want. I don't feel like over explaining myself in this sense but what i will say is that i dont want what people in academia typically want. I don't want to adopt the desires. I do want to adopt the desires of ambitious entrepreneurs, though. 

2) I care about a tangible product rather than the creation of knowledge itself (another reason why academia is not right for me). why? It feels less self-serving and ultimately, will I lie on my deathbed I think I will be happier having created a product that I feel impacted humanity in a positive way rather than strictly pursuing my own curiosity like what academia does. lmao i didnt mean to shit all over academia in this post it more about pinning down to myself why does it feel right for me. 

3) so then why biotech as opposed to anything else? I have done some thinking about this, and what I have told myself is that okay, let's start from the beginning: From when I was a kid, my mom encourage me to be a doctor (( see my about section to see more about why i decided not to pursue medicine)), but not in the sense that you must do this and it's in order. It's more like it would be cool if you did this in the most loving way possible. I kind of adopted that, and it predisposed me to liking biology, and so then I grew a genuine love for biology and then that has branched out, as I got older, into the STEM fields as a whole, but still biology on top. and since ive tested higher in math/science from a younger age, ((but as early as i can remember, this was reinforced when in 7th grade when i got a nwea score in 7th grade science of like 235 in the life sciences ( ~ 95th percentile on a quick google search) and i remember my 7th grade science teacher pulling me to the side and was like yo youre onto something here. i also )) its just been self reinforcing that like biology is for me and I think this is about as fundamental as it gets and like i think this is a good place to start for intrinsic motivation but then thinking about how to serve humanity with that is what I think will lead to most fulfillment. 

4) biotech is going to take off here soon. its the next big frontier maybe in parallel with robotics but sometime soon I have the invitation for. the giants are pouring a lot of resources into it. i dont feel like doing research to become fully defensible here, but off the top of my mind you got:
- Coefficient Bio being acquired by Anthropic in like a few months. I don't know the full context of this, but I guess, at the very least, it perhaps indicates some sort of investment in the life sciences 
- Anthropic is setting up their own wet lab. 
- OpenAI partnering with ginkgo bioworks 
- deepmind on the virtual cell mission 

5) why do my own as opposed to working at a startup. i mean like tbh im not completely ruling out working at one I a) just want to be treated like an equal and have the responsibility to shape the company's direction. ive been the one to sit out of important meetings and felt the weight of feeling replaceable and insignificant. I want to pour my all into a company and reap what i sow.  i cannot operate in a environment where i dont have autonomy and feel insignificant ie not big tech and honestly not like any established company for that matter. but its about playing probabilities, not outliers. 

6) i want to have fun with a lean team of people my age. Life is really about finding your tribe and i want that bond with a founding team. ive seen it from the outside. 

In conclusion, it was the perfect intersection of my innate interests/talent as well as where the world is going. 

((i think theres more context to fill in as to how exactly I landed on biotech which is more about my story, and I think I will go back and type more about my story in my About section when I feel like it. ))

so now i want to find a problem in biotech that i have a deep desire to solve and reverse engineer the practical path to do it. This is where I will be pouring all my efforts as of now: finding a problem i care so much about that I am willing to suffer for it. @m_goes_distance and the bio/acc movement has served as a great place for me to at least get excited about where biotech is headed even though I would have to do more thinking for myself about whether I fully resonate with the movement.

I wanted to start this is ground myself intellectually. I have realized that I am more driven by hype as of now, which is a fine place to start, but I think there needs to be honest pursuit of truth thereafter. I want to pursue truth of crazy ideas with the energy that comes with the excitement . . . i have to close my laptop for class ill complete this later

taking a stance on e/acc and equivalent movements ie bio/acc and inspiration for starting to write online. 

my initial intuition is to hop on the ideology. and, as of now, without fully thinking through them to become fully defenceable, i use them for their utility: the energy i get from the ideas of rapid tech growth that i use to dive deeper into the subject. but what ive found with myself is that i become excited by something like bio/acc, but i need to carry out thinking though it, which is why i started this blog of sorts
